subject: Emergency Generator Fuel Storage Exceeds Code Allowance for Indoor Installation
question:
The emergency generator (Drawing E-101) is located in the basement mechanical room with an integral sub-base fuel tank. The spec (Section 26 32 00) calls for a 1,000-gallon diesel tank to provide 96 hours of runtime at full load.

Per IFC Section 5704.3.3.4, the maximum allowable quantity of Class II combustible liquid (diesel) inside a building is 660 gallons without classifying the room as an H-3 occupancy.

Our 1,000-gallon tank exceeds this limit by 340 gallons.

Options:
1. Reduce tank to 660 gallons (provides only 63 hours runtime - may not meet facility requirements)
2. Relocate generator and tank to exterior pad (significant redesign, site constraints)
3. Classify the generator room as H-3 occupancy (requires 2-hour fire barriers, explosion venting, and additional fire suppression)
4. Install a 660-gallon indoor tank + 340-gallon outdoor day tank with automatic transfer
5. Request a code variance from the AHJ

The building permit was issued based on the current design. If we need to reclassify the room, this may require a permit revision and plan review, adding 4-6 weeks.

Providence Health has a 96-hour runtime requirement for their Joint Commission accreditation. We cannot reduce below this threshold.

Please advise on the preferred approach. We need to resolve this before the electrical rough-in reaches the generator room (scheduled May 20).
cost_impact: High - any option involves significant additional work
